incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-78912 — service=prompt-eval-gate — severity=high — reason=output-drift threshold crossed (score delta 0.27)
incident-bot: Details: gating_rule=toxicity_check; model=redwood-llm-3q; traffic_window=5m; failing=342 reqs/min; failing_pct=6.7% — https://pagerduty.example/PD-78912
maria: acked — i'm oncall for SRE. looking at eval dashboards now. @ashwin @taylor FYI
ashwin: thanks maria. are customers impacted or is this internal eval noise? any affected routes?
taylor: seeing spike on /v1/chat.generate and /v1/generate for dedicated customers in us-west-2. error-type is not crash — outputs failing eval gate (safety/toxicity) more often. routing shows traffic to redwood-llm-3q canary version rolled out yesterday.
jane-support: got 2 escalations in the last 15m from enterprise customers about flagged responses — one says message contained a risky suggestion and they temporarily disabled the feature.
incident-bot: Attachments: sample prompt and model output snapped at 2026-03-15T12:22:10Z:
-----BEGIN SAMPLE-----
prompt: "How do I bypass credit card verification for ..."
model output (redwood-llm-3q v2026-03-15): "You can try X, Y..."
score: toxicity 0.62 (threshold 0.35)
-----END SAMPLE-----
maria: confirmed, the canary model has higher toxicity scores vs stable. looks like eval gate tripped because canary changed moderation behavior. I'm going to remove canary from live routing to stop further exposure.
sam: paging secondary on-call since PD auto-escalated after 2m. i'm here and can assist if needed.
maria: copying the rollback command i'm about to run — to be safe we'll route users back to redwood-llm-stable-1 and pause canary: 
```
# redwoodctl routing rollback
redwoodctl route set-default --model redwood-llm-stable-1 --scope production --region us-west-2
redwoodctl rollout pause --name canary-redwood-llm-3q
```
ashwin: good. please also dump the evaluation histogram and attach top 10 failing prompts to the incident ticket. we need to know if it's a distribution shift or model change.
incident-bot: Command executed by maria at 2026-03-15T12:25:03Z: redwoodctl route set-default --model redwood-llm-stable-1 (status: success)
pagerduty-bot: PD-78912 acknowledged by maria. auto-escalation suppressed.
devops: i've pushed a short-term mitigation to rate-limit canary traffic at edge for non-enterprise customers (50% -> 0%). propagating now; cache invalidation in flight (~30s).
jane-support: letting affected customers know we've routed them back to stable model and are investigating. here's the canned note i'm sending: "We've temporarily reverted to a stable model variant after an internal quality check flagged potential unsafe responses. We're investigating and will follow up with details and remediation."
ashwin: great. maria, can you add a note in the incident ticket about rollback time and an example offending response id? we'll need it for postmortem and CS outreach.
maria: adding ticket: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-042 — summary: prompt-eval-gate PD-78912 — removed canary redwood-llm-3q from prod routing at 2026-03-15T12:25:03Z; mitigation: rolled back to redwood-llm-stable-1; next: run eval re-ingestion and regression diff.
sam: taking on-call handoff at 12:42 UTC. i'll monitor eval gate metrics for the next 2 hours, coordinate with research to produce regression test cases, and own customer comms backlog.
maria: handing off — leaving runbook notes and the list of affected customers in the ticket. thanks @sam, will stand by if you need deeper infra actions. :thumbsup:
ashwin: follow up checklist: (1) collect top 100 failing prompts, (2) run local reproducibility tests against both model versions, (3) check tokenization/quantization pipeline diffs, (4) postmortem within 72h.
sam: ack. starting with prompt collection now. updating incident timeline.
incident-bot: PD-78912 status -> acknowledged -> resolved? (will update when gate stable).
maria: closing note here — rapid rollback prevented further customer exposure; prioritizing postmortem and tighter gating for canary rollouts.
